title: How do you build a training matrix for a nursing home?
seoTitle: Training matrix for a nursing home
description: Build a nursing home training matrix: facility assessment, nurse aide in-service, licensed nurse CPD, kitchen, housekeeping and governance rows by market.
shortAnswer: A nursing home training matrix is built from the facility's own assessment of its residents and staff competencies, then mapped across every department in the building: nurse aides, licensed nurses, dietary and kitchen staff, housekeeping and maintenance, activities, volunteers, administrators and the governing body. Each row records what the residential care rules in that country require, the cycle that applies, and the record a surveyor or quality assessor will ask to see.
keyTakeaways: A residential facility is a single building with many departments, so the matrix has to reach beyond care staff to kitchen, housekeeping, maintenance, volunteers and contractors.
In the United States the facility assessment under 42 CFR 483.71 sets the amount and types of training, and must be documented and reviewed at least annually.

Some cycles are fixed: at least 12 hours of in-service a year for nurse aides, annual bloodborne pathogens training within one year of the last, and in Australia annual training on incident, complaints and whistleblower systems.

Licensed nurses carry their own professional clocks, such as one Florida contact hour per month of the licensure cycle or 20 hours a year for an Australian registered nurse, which the facility should verify rather than deliver.
As at November 2026, the repeal of the 2024 US staffing standards, the November 2026 hazard communication training deadline and a proposed Ahpra CPD standard all affect rows.

sections.heading: What makes a nursing home matrix different from a broader aged care matrix?

blocks.text: A nursing home matrix describes one residential site that runs around the clock with several departments under one roof. A broader aged care matrix, covered in [how to build a training matrix for aged care](/guides/how-to-build-a-training-matrix-for-aged-care), spans home care, hospice and community services; a nursing home matrix goes deeper into the building itself, including the kitchen, laundry, plant room, night roster and the governing body that oversees the facility.

The base method is unchanged from [how to build a training matrix](/guides/how-to-build-a-training-matrix): roles on one axis, obligations on the other, with a rule in every cell. What a residential facility adds is a department tag and a shift tag on each row, so gaps on nights and weekends show up, and a link from every row back to the facility assessment that justifies it.

sections.heading: How does the facility assessment drive the training plan?

blocks.text: In a US nursing home, the facility assessment is the starting document: 42 CFR 483.95 says the amount and types of training must be based on it. Build the matrix from the assessment, not the other way round.

items: **What the assessment contains.** Under 42 CFR 483.71 it is documented, reviewed at least annually, and covers staff competencies and personnel training, with involvement from a member of the governing body and direct care staff.

**What the matrix takes from it.** Each resident need identified in the assessment, such as dementia care or a cognitively impaired population, should map to at least one row and one competency check.

**The Australian parallel.** Outcome 2.9 of the strengthened Aged Care Quality Standards requires providers to give aged care workers training and supervision to perform their roles effectively, and the Aged Care Quality and Safety Commission's guidance describes a training matrix by role type, with training records for all workers including contractors.

sections.heading: What do residential care rules require in each market?

blocks.text: Draw the columns from the regulation pages for each country where the operator runs a facility. The summaries below rely only on those pages.

items: **United States, CMS.** 42 CFR 483.95 requires an effective training program for all new and existing staff, individuals providing services under contract and volunteers, consistent with their roles. Nurse aides need no less than 12 hours of in-service training a year, including dementia management and abuse prevention, care of cognitively impaired residents, and identified areas of weakness. Operating organizations with five or more facilities must run mandatory annual compliance and ethics training and designate a compliance officer under 483.85 ([CMS nursing home training](/regulations/cms-nursing-home-training-requirements)).

**United States, OSHA.** Employees with occupational exposure to blood or other potentially infectious materials must be trained at no cost during working hours, at initial assignment and at least annually within one year of the previous session, with material suited to their literacy and language ([bloodborne pathogens](/regulations/osha-bloodborne-pathogens-training-requirements)). Hazard communication training is due at initial assignment and whenever a new chemical hazard is introduced ([hazard communication](/regulations/osha-hazard-communication-training-requirements)).

**United States, kitchen.** Under the FDA Food Code, the person in charge must be a certified food protection manager unless the regulatory authority deems the establishment minimal risk, a person in charge must be present during all hours of operation, and employees must be trained in food safety including food allergy awareness. The Food Code is a model that each jurisdiction adopts, so confirm the version in force locally ([FDA Food Code](/regulations/fda-food-code-certified-food-protection-manager)).

**United States, licensed nurses (Florida example).** Florida requires one contact hour for each calendar month of the licensure cycle, with mandatory topics such as medical errors, laws and rules, and human trafficking each biennium ([Florida nursing CE](/regulations/florida-nursing-continuing-education)).

**Australia.** The Aged Care Act 2024 commenced on 1 November 2025. Registered providers must ensure compliance with worker screening, qualifications and training, and capability development requirements under section 152, and section 175 requires a registered nurse on site at all times ([Aged Care Act worker obligations](/regulations/aged-care-act-2024-worker-obligations)). Standards 6 and 7 of the strengthened Quality Standards apply to residential care, and core training matters in action 2.9.6 include dementia, medical emergencies and the Code of Conduct ([Aged Care Quality Standards](/regulations/aged-care-quality-standards-training)). Registered nurses and enrolled nurses complete at least 20 hours of CPD a year under the Nursing and Midwifery Board of Australia standard ([Ahpra CPD](/regulations/ahpra-cpd-registration-standards)).

sections.heading: Which nursing home cycles are fixed and which does the facility set?

blocks.text: Residential care has more fixed cycles than most sectors, but several important rows still have none. Label each interval with its source so a surveyor can tell a legal minimum from a facility choice.

items: **Fixed by rule.** Nurse aide in-service of at least 12 hours a year; bloodborne pathogens training at least annually within one year of the last; annual facility assessment review; annual compliance and ethics training for operators of five or more facilities; Australian incident, complaints and whistleblower training at least annually and on joining.
**Fixed by the professional regulator.** Florida nurses earn one contact hour per month of the licensure cycle; Australian registered nurses complete at least 20 hours of CPD a year.
**Event driven only.** Hazard communication training has no fixed refresher, and the Australian system training restarts when the relevant system changes.

**Chosen by the facility.** Outcome 2.9 and much of 483.95 require effective training consistent with roles but set no date. Document the reasoning, for example tying dementia refreshers to the resident profile in the facility assessment. See [how to set mandatory training refresh cycles](/guides/how-to-set-mandatory-training-refresh-cycles).

sections.heading: How should agency nurses, night staff and volunteers be handled?

blocks.text: Include them by name or by agency, because the rules include them. 42 CFR 483.95 covers individuals providing services under contract and volunteers, and the Aged Care Act 2024 defines aged care workers to include independent contractors and volunteers.

items: **Agency nurses.** Verify license or registration rather than delivering professional CE. In Florida, nurses practicing on a multistate license from another compact state need not complete Florida CE, so record the license type. In Australia, the NMBA offers a bulk registration check service for employers.

**Night and weekend shifts.** Add a shift tag to each row and report coverage by shift. A medical emergency competency held only by day staff is a gap, especially where section 175 requires a registered nurse on site at all times.

**Volunteers.** Give them a short, role specific row. In Australia they are aged care workers for screening and Code of Conduct purposes, and a police certificate not more than 3 years old, or a permitted alternative, is part of the entry gate.
**Competence, not attendance.** For hands on care tasks, pair the training row with a [verification of competency](/guides/how-to-set-up-verification-of-competency) step observed on the floor.

sections.heading: Which records will surveyors and quality assessors check?

blocks.text: They check that records exist for every worker type, carry the required fields and are retained for the period the rule sets. Retention periods differ sharply by rule.

items: **Australian worker records.** Aged Care Rules 2025 section 154-905 sets the contents of worker records and section 154-910 requires seven year retention.
**Bloodborne pathogens.** Training records hold dates, a content summary, trainer names and qualifications, and attendee names, and are kept three years.

**Nursing CPD.** NMBA CPD records are kept at least five years and must show learning needs, a plan, participation and reflection. Routine annual CPR and mandatory fire training cannot be counted as CPD, so keep those as separate facility rows.
**Florida CE.** Nurses report completion to CE Broker rather than submitting certificates, so the facility record should hold the verification date and result.

**Facility assessment.** CMS expects the assessment to be documented and reviewed at least annually; keep each version alongside the matrix it produced. The guide on [how long to keep training records](/guides/how-long-to-keep-training-records) compares retention rules.

sections.heading: Which 2026 and 2027 dates affect a nursing home matrix?

blocks.text: Add the dates below as future or recently changed rows. Each comes from the linked regulation pages, as at November 2026.

items: **2 February 2026, United States:** the CMS interim final rule repealing provisions of the 2024 minimum staffing rule took effect; it keeps the facility assessment at 483.71 as the reference point.

**17 September 2026, United States:** the 2026 FDA Food Code was released, adding food defense to the person in charge knowledge areas and a new food defense awareness item for employees; it applies only as jurisdictions adopt it.
**20 November 2026, United States:** employers must update hazard communication labeling, programs and training as necessary for substances, with the mixtures deadline on 19 May 2028.
**30 April 2027, Florida:** registered nurse license Group 3 expires, so CE verification for that group should be complete before then.

blocks.title: Proposed, not yet in force
blocks.text: Ahpra and 14 National Boards consulted from 15 May to 17 July 2026 on revised recency of practice and CPD standards, including a draft requirement of 20 hours with 5 interactive hours. Keep the current NMBA standard in the matrix and track the draft as a watch item.

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry links each nursing home obligation to the department and role it applies to, the resident needs in the facility assessment, and the assessment point that shows competence, so a revised assessment or a new Food Code edition flags the affected rows. See [healthcare and life sciences](/industries/healthcare-life-sciences).

faqs.q: What must a nurse aide's annual in-service training include?
faqs.a: Under 42 CFR 483.95(g), at least 12 hours a year, covering dementia management and abuse prevention, areas of weakness, and care of cognitively impaired residents where relevant. The facility assessment should shape the remaining content, and the matrix should record hours by topic, not just a total.

faqs.q: Does routine CPR training count toward an Australian nurse's CPD hours?
faqs.a: No. The Nursing and Midwifery Board of Australia states that routine annual CPR and mandatory fire training cannot be counted toward the CPD minimum. Keep them as facility rows with their own cycle, and keep CPD as a separate professional row that the facility verifies.

faqs.q: Do agency nurses working in a Florida nursing home need Florida CE?
faqs.a: Not if they practice on a multistate license issued by another Nurse Licensure Compact state. Nurses holding a Florida license must meet Florida CE, including the mandatory topics. Record the license type for every agency nurse so the matrix applies the right rule.

faqs.q: Which nursing home operators need annual compliance and ethics training?
faqs.a: Under 42 CFR 483.85, operating organizations with five or more facilities must have mandatory annual compliance and ethics training meeting 483.95(f) and a designated compliance officer. Single site operators still need a compliance program, but the annual training requirement is tied to the five facility threshold.
